cases.purpose: Independent Tcl Expect positive 3-second deadline under continuing nonmatching output. The producer waits for go, writes x every 50 ms, logs monotonic emission timestamps, and terminates only after stop or a 7-second failure bound. The independent Expect second-resolution window is 1.9 <= elapsed < 4.0 seconds; the existing -t 1 candidate contract retains its tighter bound.
cases.stdout:
controller-exit-zero=PASS
controller-no-diagnostics=PASS
ready-match=PASS
whole-wait-timeout-status-one=PASS
whole-wait-1.9-to-4-seconds=PASS
producer-continuous-for-at-least-1.8-seconds=PASS
producer-stopped-by-command-after-wait=PASS
close-zero=PASS

files.expect-deadline.sh:
expect log_user off
exec 5>"$HOME/expect.raw"
exec 6>"$HOME/metrics"
rec() { printf '%s=%s\n' "$1" "$2" >&6; }
expect spawn /usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/terminal-review-observer.py producer stream -h fd -h pid
expect log "$fd" -F 5 -m
expect expect "$fd" READY -t 4; rec ready "$?"
expect sendline "$fd" go
t0=${EPOCHREALTIME/./}
expect expect "$fd" NEVER_MATCH_THIS -t 3; r=$?
t1=${EPOCHREALTIME/./}
rec wait "$r"
rec elapsed_ms "$(( (t1 - t0) / 1000 ))"
expect sendline "$fd" stop
expect eof "$fd" -t 3
expect close "$fd" "$pid"; rec close "$?"
exec 5>&- 6>&-
exit 0

cases.oracle: Independent /usr/bin/expect (Tcl Expect 5.45.4 on sealed vm-cache-reference-tools). timeout/eof events map to documented expect 1/2 and eof 1/0 statuses. cases.purpose: Interrupt an owned child with trapped SIGUSR1 only after observing its actual clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_MONOTONIC,0) syscall for at least 250 ms. Assert failure 1, one handler invocation, continued shell, no diagnostic, and elapsed 0.2 <= t < 1.5 seconds for the requested 2 seconds. Independent libc setup verifies the same causal driver and EINTR return convention.

sleep-returned-failure-one=PASS
shell-continued=PASS
clock-stdout-exact=PASS
signal-after-observed-clock-nanosleep=PASS
handler-once=PASS
interrupted-in-0.2-to-1.5-seconds=PASS
EINTR-no-diagnostic=PASS

files.clock-USR1.sh:
trap 'printf "handler=USR1\n"' USR1
printf "armed\n"
bashclock sleep 2
r=$?
printf "sleep-status=%s\nshell-continued\n" "$r"

cases.oracle: Independent libc clock_nanosleep called through ctypes, with errno deliberately set to ENOTTY, plus a real owned-child signal or the same stateless EINVAL filter. The API returns an error number without setting errno. The Bash contract requires return failure on EINTR, no spurious diagnostic, honouring handlers/SIGINT; other errors require the text of the returned error. This is an explicit API contract comparison, not a claim that GNU bash has a bashclock builtin.
cases.comparison: Explicit semantic/status/elapsed/diagnostic checks versus an independent libc control. Native return number, errno sentinel, syscall samples, signal time and unmodified stdout/stderr are separate diagnostic artifacts; mismatches return 1.
